I have been thinking about building a website that has a similar user experience to Voat, but with content fed by RSS feeds rather than submissions. Users would be able to create topic specific domains like subverses. If you wanted to create a topic domain you would name it then build and curate a list of RSS feeds that will display for people viewing your topic. Users could subscribe to the topics to customize the articles that are featured on their main page, just like we do here at Voat.

I really like voat's expansion button that expands the text or image into view in-line with the rest of the page without reloading, so I'd do something similar for my site. I'd show the titles of the RSS feeds articles in rows. Clicking an expansion button would bring the RSS' summary of the article along with any images into view. Links to user discussion and the source of the article would also be included.

Up and down vote options would be displayed only for users who expanded the summary. It would be interesting to apply a sort algorithm that sprinkles a combination of the newest articles, most read(expanded) articles, and most up-voted articles toward the top of the main page and each topic domain. That would make sure there is a good mix of interesting articles while giving new articles a chance to move up.

I realize this is a short pitch for a somewhat complicated website, but I didn't think you all would want to read a giant wall of text. Also, I think being on voat you can probably imagine a similar site driven by RSS.

So, what do you guys think? I'm afraid this is an idea that is scratching an itch only I have and wouldn't generate much interest so don't spare my feelings. If this is one of my dumb ideas that someone needs to talk me out of before I waste a bunch of time and money on, now is a great time. If you think its worth following up on, do you have any ideas to share?

Fig and raisin mead, just racked to secondary on oak. Recipe in comments.

Recipe for 1 gallon:

  • 3 # Wildflower honey sourced from Eagle Ridge Apiaries near Vandalia/Dayton OH

  • 1.5# Black mission figs, de-stemmed, halved and added in primary (not boiled)

  • A handful (30ish?) of raisins added in primary (again, not boiled)

  • 1 tsp pectic enzyme

  • Lalvin 71B-1122 Yeast

Let it sit 1 month in the primary, guesstimating that it will take another month on .2oz of Hungarian oak cubes (medium toast) to achieve the oak I want. After oakiness is achieved, will continue to let mead sit (sans oak) until it's 6 months old, then it will be bottled; hopefully hitting the December deadline.

OG reading was FUBAR as I jumped the gun on measuring, and the must was too warm. Even if the OG was accurate, the FG would still be inaccurate, as IDK how much sugar the figs would have introduced.
What a lovely color! Is that coming from the figs, the raisins or the oak (or all of the above)?

It's the figs providing the color, since the oak was just introduced when I took the pic.

Black mission figs (when ripe) have a very nice, mellow pinkish/reddish internal color, with a custardy texture.
